item.title: How Saima Saleem, a Pakistani Diplomat, Turned Adversity Into Strength
item.description:
Doing something no one else has done should be both fearful and exciting, right? It was just the culmination of taking an exam and finishing well, in Saima Saleem’s view.
Saleem, until recently a diplomat for Pakistan’s mission to the United Nations, was interviewed in PassBlue’s office in the UN in October about working with a disability and how she has navigated multiple postings as a career diplomat across decades.

item.title: Will Bangladesh’s Islamists Reconcile with the Nation’s Cultural Identity?
item.description: Ex cultu robur: from culture comes strength

item.title: Yemen war: Emergency aid chief calls for access to war-hit communities
item.description: The UN’s top aid official, Tom Fletcher, arrived in Yemen on Wednesday warning that the war there is preventing families from accessing the food and medicine they need to survive, particularly those in Taiz City.

item.title: Türk warns of widening risk of atrocity crimes against Palestinians
item.description: UN human rights chief Volker Türk on Wednesday warned of a widening risk of further atrocity crimes by Israel against Palestinians, saying violence in the occupied West Bank in recent months has heightened existential fears.

item.title: Governments and experts gather in Nairobi to tackle the global housing crisis
item.description: A home is a place where people can feel safe. Yet billions worldwide do not have a proper place to live. As the global housing crisis deepens, government representatives and housing experts are gathering at the United Nations in Nairobi from 26-27 November to discuss how to address it.

item.title: Gaza’s widows raise their families alone: ‘We do our duties twice over, but where are our rights?’
item.description: For women in Gaza who lost their husbands in the war, providing for a family no longer means just putting food on the table. Now it also means finding shelter, hauling water and keeping children in school – all from a tent.

item.title: Gisèle Pelicot’s son: ‘Not being violent is the bare minimum’
item.description: Two years after the Mazan rape trial, David Pelicot has decided to put his name to the fight against sexual violence – and to confront what he calls the silence of men.

item.title: Somalia: Famine risk decreases in Baidoa – but millions still going hungry
item.description: Millions of people in Somalia still face severe food shortages and malnutrition despite the reduced risk of famine in Baidoa, global food security experts warned on Wednesday.

item.title: Multilateralism Needs a New Deal, Can Anyone Deliver it?
item.description: The latest straw poll for the head of the United Nations has again proved inconclusive. The lack of a credible candidate to run the troubled institution bodes ill for repairing a fractured system of international cooperation.
